title: runtime/scheduler: cap tail latency under bursty workloads (load-shedding hook + fairness tweak)
author: Julian Moore
release_notes: Scheduler: add controlled load-shedding path and fairness tweak to reduce p99 under bursty concurrency; emits new counters for baseline explainability.
description:
Context
Baseline Run 1 surfaced a repeatable p99 blow-up on the BURSTY_CONCURRENCY + MIXED_PROMPT_LENGTHS traffic shape (streaming + non-streaming mix) when the scheduler queue crosses a threshold and decode-heavy tenants monopolize GPU time. This manifested as long queue-wait for short prefill requests and a small number of requests sitting behind large decode batches.

This PR implements two changes to cap tail latency under bursty load:
1) Load-shedding hook (soft) at the scheduler ingress, driven by queue pressure + budgeted queue-wait, to fail fast *before* we create unbounded backlog.
2) A fairness tweak in batch formation that prevents decode-only work from starving prefill under burst, while staying within our throughput budget.

High-level behavior
- When queue pressure is low/normal: behavior should be unchanged.
- When queue pressure exceeds threshold: new admission controller rejects a small fraction of requests with a structured error (429) + Retry-After, instead of letting p99 drift to multi-second queue-wait.
- Batch selection: enforce a minimum prefill slice per scheduling round (bounded) so short prompts can start prefill even when decode backlog is large.

Implementation notes
- Load-shedding is implemented as a hook in the scheduler ingress (not the API gateway) so it keys off runtime-specific pressure signals (queue depth, estimated GPU time, and queue-wait histogram buckets).
- Rejection policy is tenant-aware: we preserve in-flight requests and avoid shedding from dedicated/SLA tiers by default (configurable).
- Fairness tweak is intentionally conservative: it does not change continuous batching mechanics; it only adjusts candidate selection to avoid pathological decode dominance.

Config
- New flags (all default off in prod until rollout):
  - scheduler.admission_control.enabled
  - scheduler.admission_control.queue_depth_threshold
  - scheduler.admission_control.max_queue_wait_ms
  - scheduler.fairness.min_prefill_fraction
  - scheduler.fairness.max_prefill_burst_tokens

Metrics
Adds counters/histograms required for baseline explainability and for SRE alerting:
- scheduler_admission_rejected_total{reason,tier}
- scheduler_queue_wait_ms (existing histogram, now tagged with phase=ingress/admitted)
- scheduler_round_prefill_tokens / scheduler_round_decode_tokens
- scheduler_fairness_prefill_forced_rounds_total

Perf
On the baseline harness traffic shape (BURSTY_CONCURRENCY v1) we see p99 E2E latency cap at ~1.3-1.6s (was 3-5s) under the same offered load, with ~1-3% requests rejected at peak burst (instead of >0% timing out upstream). Throughput impact is within noise for non-burst workloads; under burst, throughput stabilizes because the queue doesn’t explode.

Risk / rollout
- Flagged + default-off.
- Rollout plan: enable on perf-canary nightly in one region, then small production slice for hosted tier only, then dedicated opt-in.

Test plan
- Unit tests for admission controller thresholds and tier routing
- Integration test with synthetic burst generator
- Ran benchmark harness locally (shape: bursty-64, mixed prompts) and validated queue-wait / rejected counters

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4831 (Run 1 anomalies), ENG-4824 (scheduler instrumentation)
- Support: SUP-9188 (throughput drop under bursty concurrency)

conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): The direction makes sense, but I’m worried about changing semantics by returning 429 from runtime. Can we ensure gateway mapping doesn’t accidentally turn this into a generic 500 for some clients? Also: fairness tweak needs a guardrail so we don’t over-prefill and tank throughput on decode-heavy steady state.

Julian Moore (author): Good call. I added explicit error mapping in runtime/http/error_mapping.cc and a proto enum so we preserve 429 + Retry-After. For fairness, I’ve added max_prefill_burst_tokens and a min_prefill_fraction cap (both flags). Defaults keep behavior unchanged unless enabled.

Noah Patel (review): On the admission controller, the queue-depth threshold alone seems brittle across SKUs. Can we key off estimated queue-wait instead (or at least include it)? Also please add metric tags so we can correlate in baseline dashboards.

Julian Moore (author): Updated to use max_queue_wait_ms as primary trigger with queue_depth_threshold as backstop. Added scheduler_queue_wait_ms tagging phase=ingress/admitted and rejection reason tags (queue_wait_exceeded, queue_depth_exceeded, tier_exempt).

Sean Gallagher (review): From an SRE perspective, we need to be explicit about paging implications. When enabled, rejecting requests isn’t an incident by itself. Please include guidance on acceptable rejection rates + where to alert.

Julian Moore (author): Added operational notes in docs/internal/runtime/scheduler/admission-control.md, including suggested alerting: warn at 0.5% sustained for hosted tier, page at 2% sustained + p99 regression. Also notes to validate driver/CUDA pins when we see sudden shifts.

Allison Grant (review): One more: metric cardinality. The new labels look okay but do not tag by model. Ensure it stays tier/reason only.

Julian Moore (author): Confirmed: no model label. Only reason + tier.

Sofia Ivanova (final): Approved with flags default-off. Let’s make sure perf-canary enables this only for the bursty shape first.

Merge: Squash merged after green CI.
